blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Recorded sessions between users and coding agents offer a way to evaluate how agents complete real-world tasks and interact with users. However, these sessions cannot simply be replayed with new agents, because recorded user replies may no longer apply when an agent takes a different trajectory. We introduce SWE-WhatIf, which replays recorded sessions with new agents by modeling the user's intents, the criteria for satisfying them, and the conditions under which they arise. Using this model, a user simulator generates replies that adapt to unseen agent turns while remaining grounded in the recording. Across 89 real-world sessions, SWE-WhatIf generated the replies most similar to those of real users and matched the strongest baseline when sessions were rewritten. To test adaptation, we replay sessions with agents instructed to avoid or repeat actions that the recorded user pushed back on. SWE-WhatIf produced the highest win rate for avoiding these actions (66.3%), significantly above chance. We further demonstrate its utility by ranking five LLMs as coding agents, where the highest-ranked model depended on how users specified and developed their intents, and a study with 16 users, where replaying their own sessions changed 14 participants' rankings and informed their future agent use.
blocks.zh: 用户和编码代理之间录制的会话提供了一个评估代理如何完成现实世界的任务并与用户互动的方法. 然而,这些会话不能简单地用新代理重放,因为当代理采取不同的轨迹时,记录的用户回复可能不再适用. 我们介绍 SWE-What If,它通过模拟用户的意图,满足的标准,以及产生这些目的的条件,与新代理重播录制的会话. 使用这个模型,一个用户模拟器生成的回复会适应不见的代理转折,而同时又被固定在录音中. 在89个现实世界会议上,SWE-What如果生成的答复与实际用户的答复最相类似,并匹配重写会议时最强的基准。 为了测试适应性,我们与被指示避免或重复被记录的用户所后推的动作的代理重放会话. SWE-What如果产生了避免这些行动的最高赢取率(66.3%),大大高于机会。 我们进一步证明了它的效用,将5个LLMs列为编码代理,其中排名最高的模型取决于用户如何说明并发展出他们的意图,还有一项有16个用户参与的研究,其中重播自己的会话改变了14位参与者的排名并告知了他们未来的代理用途.

blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.zh: 图 1:以三种代理方式模拟录制会话的示例. SWE-What如果从录制的会话(顶部)中构建用户的意向模型,模拟用户会从这个模型(底部)中回复每个代理的转折.

blocks.en:
Developers increasingly use coding agents in real-world practice.
Recent datasets release recordings of these sessions (e.g., SWE-chat ( Baumann et al., 2026 ) , DataClaw ( DataClaw contributors, 2026 ) ) that capture both the work users ask agents to do and how they steer them: what outcomes or information they request, what work they accept or reject, and what leads them to change direction or give up.
If we could replay these sessions with new agents, agents could be evaluated on their capability to complete real-world tasks while following real users’ steering, and users could test which agent best suits their own work.
blocks.zh:
开发者在现实世界实践中越来越多地使用编码代理.
最近的数据集发布这些会议的录音(如SWE-chat(Baumann等人,2026年)).,Data Claw(DataClaw 撰稿人,2026年),它既能捕捉工作用户要求代理商做,又能如何引导他们:他们要求的结果或信息,他们接受或拒绝什么工作,以及是什么导致他们改变方向或放弃.
如果我们能与新的代理商重播这些会话, 代理商可以被评价他们完成现实世界任务的能力,

blocks.en:
However, to replay a session, simply resending the user’s recorded messages to an agent is not enough.
Each message responds to what the recorded agent did, like a user correcting an agent for prematurely committing a code change.
If a new agent diverges from this observed trajectory (e.g., does not commit the code early), the real user would have replied differently, and the recorded message would no longer match the conversation.
Prior user simulators can respond to unseen agent trajectories ( Yao et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2025 ; Vijayvargiya et al., 2026 ; Laban et al., 2026 ; Raghavendra et al., 2026 ; Trinh et al., 2026 ) , but typically follow synthetic goals or personas that do not capture a particular user’s work or steering.
SWE-Together ( Wu et al., 2026b ) instead derives a simulator from a conditional script of the user’s recorded messages, which can choose when to send each message to a new agent but is constrained to their recorded content and order.
Thus, a replay needs a simulator that can adapt to trajectories that the recorded agent never took while remaining faithful to why and how the real user steered it.
blocks.zh:
然而,要重播一个会话,仅仅将用户录制的电文重新发送给代理人是不够的.
每条消息都响应了被记录的代理的行为,比如用户纠正代理过早地执行代码更改.
如果新代理偏离了这个观测到的轨迹(例如,不提前执行代码),则真正的用户会做出不同的答复,录制的消息将不再匹配对话.
先前的用户模拟器可以对隐形物剂轨迹作出反应(姚等人,2025年;吴等人,2025年;Vijayvargiya等人,2026年;Laban等人,2026年;Raghavendra等人,2026年;Trinh等人,2026年),但一般遵循合成目标或人物,不捕捉特定用户的工作或方向.
SWE-Together(Wu et al., 2026b)转而从用户录制消息的有条件脚本中获取一个模拟器,可以选择何时向新代理发送每条消息,但受其录制内容和顺序的限制.
因此,重播需要一个模拟器,可以适应被录制的代理商从未使用过的轨迹,同时忠于为什么和真实的用户如何引导它.

blocks.en:
We introduce SWE-WhatIf , a framework that turns a recorded session into a replay task for new coding agents.
Instead of a script of the recorded replies, SWE-WhatIf extracts an intent model : the outcomes or information the user wanted ( intents ), the criteria by which they accepted or rejected the agent’s work, and the conditions under which each intent was raised or dropped.
During replay, the simulator tracks these intents and, after each agent turn, judges the agent’s actions against their criteria and conditions, updates the intent state, and generates the user’s next reply based on this state.
As a result, the simulator reacts to what the new agent actually did based on reasons grounded in the recording (e.g., objecting to a commit only if it is actually early).
blocks.zh:
我们引入了 SWE-What If ,这个框架将一个录制的会话变成一个新的编码代理的重播任务.
SWE-What If提取意图模型:用户想要的结果或信息(意图),他们接受或拒绝代理人工作的标准,以及提出或放弃每项意图的条件。
在重播时,模拟器会跟踪这些意图,并在每个代理商转身后,根据代理商的标准和条件判断代理商的行为,更新意向状态,并生成用户基于此状态的下一个回复.
因此,模拟器对新代理根据记录中基于的理由(例如,只有在实际很早的情况下才反对一项承诺)实际所做的反应.

blocks.en:
We evaluate SWE-WhatIf both intrinsically, by testing its faithful adaptability against three other user simulators, and extrinsically, by demonstrating its utility in two applications.
For the intrinsic evaluation, we use 89 real-world sessions released by SWE-Together ( Wu et al., 2026b ) and SWE-chat ( Baumann et al., 2026 ) .
For replication and robustness, we compare simulated replies with real users’ replies on the original recordings and on versions rewritten in form but not in content. SWE-WhatIf generated the most similar replies on the recordings, while matching the best baseline on the rewritten sessions.
For adaptation, we replay each session with an agent instructed to avoid actions that the real user pushed back on and another instructed to repeat them.
With SWE-WhatIf , the former agent achieved the highest win rate among the simulators in terms of task success and user burden, significantly above chance.
blocks.zh:
我们从本质上评估SWE-What如果两者,通过测试其忠实的适应性以对抗其他三个用户模拟器,并通过在两个应用中展示其效用来进行外部评估。
对于内在评价,我们使用由SWE-Together(Wu等人,2026b)和SWE-chat(Baumann等人,2026)发布的89个现实世界会话.
为了复制和坚固,我们将模拟答复与真实用户对原始录音和形式重写但内容不重写的版本的答复进行比较。 SWE-What如果在录音中产生最相似的答复,同时匹配重写会话的最佳基线.
为了适应,我们每场比赛都要重播一次,由一位代理人指示避免真正的用户推后的行动,另一位则指示重复.
与 SWE-What If 相比,前代理在任务成功和用户负担方面在模拟器中实现了最高的赢率,大大高于机会.

blocks.en:
For the extrinsic evaluation, we first use SWE-WhatIf to replay 58 tasks with five LLMs as coding agents in the same harness ( Anomaly, 2025 ) .
Our ranking agreed more closely with Agent Arena’s ranking from real-user sessions than with the other published rankings.
The rankings also differed based on how users steered the agents (e.g., giving details upfront or raising requests only in certain situations).
We then study whether replaying developers’ own sessions can help them decide which coding agents to use and how to use them.
In a user study, 16 coding-agent users provided their own sessions and reviewed simulated replays with three different agents.
After reading the replays, 14 of 16 participants changed how they initially ranked the agents, including 10 who changed their top-ranked agent.
From the replays, participants also reported gaining insights for their future agent use—e.g., when cheaper models were sufficient, how each agent works differently, and how to steer agents.
blocks.zh:
对于外部评价,我们首先使用SWE-What(如果用5个LLMs作为编码剂)重播58项任务(Anomaly,2025年)。
我们的排名比其他公布的排名更接近于Arena探员从实际用户会话中的排名。
排名也因用户如何指导代理而有所不同(例如,在某些情况下提供细节或仅提出请求)。
然后我们研究重新播放开发者自己的会话是否有助于他们决定要使用的编码代理以及如何使用它们.
在一项用户研究中,16个编码代理用户提供了自己的会话,并审查了三种不同代理的模拟重播.
在读完重播后,16位参与者中有14位改变了他们最初对代理的排名,包括10位更换了排名最高的代理.
从重播中,与会者还报告说,他们对未来的制剂使用有了深刻的认识,例如,当廉价的型号足够时,每种制剂如何不同地工作,如何引导制剂。

blocks.en: 2 SWE-WhatIf
blocks.zh: 2 如果

blocks.en: 2.1 Task Definition
blocks.zh: 2.1 任务定义

blocks.en:
SWE-WhatIf creates a replay task from a recorded session (i.e., user messages, agent messages, and tool calls) and its starting environment (i.e., code repository and runtime when the session began).
In this task, a new agent is given the starting environment and the user’s opening request, and it must complete the user’s work from the recorded session while interacting turn by turn with a user simulator that steers it as the original user would.
As the new agent can take any path, the simulator must respond to actions absent from the recording, but only in ways supported by the user’s recorded requests and reactions.
We refer to this as faithful adaptability .
blocks.zh:
SWE-What 如果从一个录制的会话(即用户消息,代理消息,和工具呼叫)及其起始环境(即代码寄存器和会话开始时的运行时间)创建重播任务.
在此任务中,给予新代理商初始环境和用户的开机请求,它必须完成从录制会话开始的用户工作,同时依次与按原用户方向引导的用户模拟器进行交替互动.
由于新代理可以走任何路径,模拟器必须响应录制中缺失的动作,但只能以用户所记录的请求和反应支持的方式.
我们称之为忠实的适应能力。

blocks.en: 2.2 User Simulator
blocks.zh: 2.2 用户模拟器

blocks.en:
Inspired by prior work on user simulators driven by representations of user intents ( Schatzmann et al., 2007 ; Kim et al., 2026 ; Tack et al., 2026 ) , SWE-WhatIf builds an intent model from the recording to represent the outcomes the user sought and the conditions under which they raised or dropped requests.
During replay, the simulator uses this model to decide which requests and reactions apply to the new agent’s actions.
blocks.zh:
受用户意向表达推动的用户模拟器的前期工作启发(Schatzmann等人,2007年;Kim等人,2026年;Tack等人,2026年),SWE-Whatif从录制中建立意向模型,以代表用户寻求的结果以及他们提出或放弃请求的条件.
在重播期间,模拟器使用这个模型来决定哪些请求和反应适用于新代理的行为.

blocks.en:
The intent model describes the user’s work as outcomes rather than turns.
The model consists of a set of intents , each an outcome or piece of information that the user wanted during the session (e.g., a bug fixed, an explanation of why a test fails).
Each intent has criteria that define what is needed to satisfy it (e.g., the fix must not skip the failing test).
Each intent can also have conditions that capture what led the user to raise it: a dependency on another intent (e.g., creating a test after implementing a feature), a situation that arose in the session (e.g., a test failing), or information that the user gained from the agent (e.g., the agent’s assessment of a proposed fix).
Conditions can also capture when the user drops an intent (e.g., a new fact leads them to give up one approach for another).
Every criterion and condition is grounded in the user’s own turns or in outcomes that they implicitly accepted.
blocks.zh:
意图模式将用户的工作描述为成果而非转折.
模型由一组意图组成,每个结果或用户在会话中想要的信息(例如一个bug固定,解释测试失败的原因).
每个意图都有标准来定义满足它所需要的内容(例如,定点不能跳过失败的测试).
每种意图还可以有能够捕捉导致用户提出它的条件:对另一种意图的依赖(例如,实施一个特性后产生测试),会场中出现的情况(例如,测试失败),或用户从代理人那里获得的信息(例如,代理人对拟议定律的评估).
条件也可以在用户放弃某种意图时捕捉到(例如,一个新事实导致他们放弃一种方法而放弃另一种方法).
每个标准和条件都基于用户自己的回合或他们默示接受的结果。

blocks.en:
During a replay, the user simulator tracks and updates the state of the intents in the model at each turn.
Each intent is blocked (i.e., its conditions are not yet met), open (i.e., the simulated user can now express it), raised (i.e., the simulated user has expressed it), dropped (i.e., it no longer applies), or abandoned (i.e., the agent has stopped making progress on it, so the simulated user gives up).
Separately, each criterion of an intent is either met or unmet , so an intent can be fully, partly, or not yet satisfied.
At the start of a replay, the intents in the user’s opening request are already raised.
blocks.zh:
在重播期间,用户模拟器跟踪并更新每个回合模型中意图的状态.
每个意图被屏蔽(即其条件尚未满足),开放(即模拟用户现在可以表达),提升(即模拟用户已经表达),放弃(即不再适用),或放弃(即代理已经停止在它上取得进展,因此模拟用户放弃).
另外,意图的每一项标准要么得到满足,要么未得到满足,因此意图可以完全、部分或尚未得到满足。
在重播开始时,用户开机请求中的意图已经提出.

blocks.en: To generate each reply as the user would, the simulator also uses a style profile computed from the user’s messages in the recording (e.g., length, punctuation, formality).
blocks.zh: 要按照用户的意愿生成每个回复,模拟器还使用从记录中用户消息中计算出来的样式配置(如长度,标点,形式).

blocks.en:
SWE-WhatIf builds the intent model with LLM-based agents that draft, review, and revise it.
A drafting agent reads all user messages in the recorded session and groups them into intents with their criteria and conditions.
A reviewing agent then checks the draft for issues, such as overly prescriptive criteria that would penalize functionally equivalent approaches (e.g., requiring a particular function name) or criteria and conditions that cannot be satisfied in a replay (e.g., requiring an external private API).
A final agent revises the draft based on this review.
The style profile is computed directly from the user’s messages.
Further details are in Appendix A.1 , and an example intent model is in Appendix A.3 .
blocks.zh:
SWE-What如果用LLM的代理来建立意图模型,负责起草、审查和修订。
一个起草机构在录制的会话中读取所有用户信息,并将其与其标准和条件组合成意向.
然后由审查人员检查草案中的问题,例如过于规范性的标准将惩罚功能等同的方法(例如要求特定函数名称)或不能在重播中满足的标准和条件(例如要求外部私人API).
最终代理人根据这一审查对草案进行修订。
样式配置直接从用户信件中计算。
进一步详情见附录A.1,附录A.3为意图模式。

blocks.en: 2.3 Turn-by-Turn Simulation
blocks.zh: 2.3 转弯模拟

blocks.en: Figure 2: After Agent B’s turn in Figure 1 , the simulator responds by (1) assessing the criteria of the raised intents and the conditions of blocked intents against the agent’s turn, (2) updating the intent states accordingly, and (3) responding by deciding which intents to express in the next message and writing this message in the user’s style.
blocks.zh: 图2:在Agent B在图1中交接后,模拟器的反应是:(1) 评估所提出意图的标准以及阻止意图的条件与Agent的交接相比,(2) 对意图进行相应更新,(3) 作出反应时决定哪些意图在下一个信息中表示,并以用户的风格写下这一信息。

blocks.en:
After each agent turn, our user simulator takes three steps to generate a message (Fig. 2 ). (1) Assess: Inspired by LLM-as-a-Judge approaches ( Zheng et al., 2023 ; Ye et al., 2024 ; Kim et al., 2024 ; Viswanathan et al., 2025 ) , we use an LLM to judge the agent’s actions and message against the criteria of the raised intents and the conditions of the blocked intents. (2) Update: Then, based on the judgments, the simulator updates each intent’s state (e.g., an intent becomes open when its conditions are met, or abandoned if its criteria do not change for several turns). (3) Respond: An LLM selects which intents to express next and writes the user’s reply, guided by the style profile.
The replay ends when every intent is satisfied, dropped, or abandoned, or when no intent changes state for several consecutive turns (details in Appendix A.2 ).
blocks.zh:
每个代理转弯后,我们的用户模拟器会采取三个步骤生成一个消息(图2). (1) 评估:在LLM-as-judge方法的启发下(Zheng等人,2023年;Ye等人,2024年;Kim等人,2024年;Viswanathan等人,2025年),我们使用LLM来判断代理人的行为和信息,以判断所提出的意图的标准和被封锁的意图的条件. (2)更新:然后,根据判断,模拟器更新每个意图的状态(例如,一个意图在满足其条件时就会开放,或者如果其标准不改变几个回合就放弃). (3) 答复: LLM 选择要表达下一个并写用户的回复, 并遵循样式配置 。
重播在满足、放弃或放弃每一项意图,或连续几个回合没有改变意图时结束(详见附录A.2)。

blocks.en: 2.4 Scoring a Replay
blocks.zh: 2.4 重新计分

blocks.en:
We score each replay on two aspects: success (i.e., whether the new agent completed the user’s work) and user burden , since two replays can reach the same outcome but one can require more steering from the user ( Shen et al., 2026 ) .
To judge success, we adapt the goal-based judging used in SWE-Together ( Wu et al., 2026b ) : an LLM writes a list of goals for each task from the recorded session alone, and an LLM judge marks each goal as met or not met from the replay’s final state (i.e., repository changes and the agent’s messages).
We calculate the percentage of goals met as success, s s .
To account for burden, we multiply s s by ( n real + 1 ) / ( n sim + 1 ) (n_{\mathrm{real}}+1)/(n_{\mathrm{sim}}+1) , where n sim n_{\mathrm{sim}} and n real n_{\mathrm{real}} are the numbers of messages that the simulated user and the real user sent after the opening request.
This burden-adjusted success penalizes a replay that needed more messages than the real session and rewards one that needed fewer.
blocks.zh:
我们每个重播的得分分为两个方面:成功(即新代理是否完成了用户的工作)和用户负担,因为两个重播可以达到相同的结果,但一个可以要求用户提供更多的指导(Shen等人,2026年).
为了判断成功与否,我们调整了SWE-Together(Wu等人,2026年b)中使用的基于目标的判断:一个LLM为每个任务单写一个目标列表,一个LLM法官将每个目标标注为从重播的最终状态(即寄存器的更改和代理消息)中达到或未达到的目标.
我们计算成功的目标的百分比。
为了说明负担,我们将 s 乘以 (n real + 1) / (n sim + 1) (n_{\mathrm{ real}}+1)/(n_{\mathrm{sim}}+1),其中n sim n_{\mathrm{sim}}和n real real n_{\mathrm{real}}是模拟用户和在开机请求后真实用户发送的信息数量.
这种经过负担调整的成功将惩罚需要比实际会议更多信息的重播,并奖励需要更少的信息。

blocks.en: 3 User Simulator Validation
blocks.zh: 3 用户模拟验证

blocks.en:
To validate our user simulator, we evaluate three dimensions of faithful adaptability .
First, the simulator should reproduce the real user’s behavior in the recorded sessions ( replication ).
Second, it should keep this behavior when a session changes in form but not in content ( robustness ), such as when turns are paraphrased.
Finally, when the agent’s trajectory changes in content, the simulator should respond differently but only as the user would ( adaptation ).
blocks.zh:
为了验证我们的用户模拟器,我们评价忠实适应性的三个方面。
首先,模拟器应该在录制的会话中复制真实用户的行为(复制).
第二,当一个会话在形式上有所改变,但在内容上却没有变化(强健性)时,例如转弯时,它应该保持这种行为.
最后,当代理商的轨迹改变内容时,模拟器应该做出不同的反应,但只能像用户那样(适应).

blocks.en:
To evaluate these dimensions, we build tests from the recorded sessions.
For replication, we follow prior work ( Dou et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2026a ) and compare each simulator’s reply with the real user’s reply at each point of a session.
For robustness, we repeat this comparison on versions of the sessions with turns paraphrased and merged.
For adaptation, the recorded session does not show how the user would reply to a different agent, and an agent can depart from the recording in too many ways to test each one.
However, the session reveals agent actions that the user pushed back on (e.g., a change that was later undone), and if the agent had avoided such an action, the user would not have needed to push back.
Based on this, we replay each session with an agent that repeats these actions and one that proactively avoids them, where a faithful simulator should produce replays with the latter agent that achieve higher burden-adjusted success.
blocks.zh:
为了评估这些方面,我们从记录的会议中进行测试。
为了复制,我们遵循先前的工作(Dou等人,2025年;Wu等人,2026年a),并将每个模拟器的答复与实际用户在会话每一点的答复进行比较。
为了稳健性,我们重复对会议版本的这种比较,转而加以解释和合并。
为了适应,录制的会话没有显示用户会如何回复不同的代理,一个代理可以以太多的方式离开录制,以测试每个代理.
然而,会话揭示了用户推后进行的代理动作(如后来被撤销的更改),如果代理避免了这样的动作,用户就不需要推后了.
在此基础上,我们每场会话都会与一个重复这些行动的代理重放,并主动回避,一个忠实的模拟器应该与后一种代理重放,实现更高的负重调整成功.

blocks.en:
These evaluations test SWE-WhatIf intrinsically .
We also conduct extrinsic evaluations to demonstrate the framework’s utility: ranking LLMs as coding agents and examining how their rankings vary across sessions (§ 4 ), and studying whether replays of their own sessions can help users decide which agents to use and how to use them (§ 5 ).
blocks.zh:
这些评价检验了SWE-如果本质上是什么。
我们还进行外部评价,以展示框架的效用:将LLMs列为编码代理商,并研究其排名如何因会议而异(第4节),并研究自己会议的重播是否能够帮助用户决定使用哪些代理商以及如何使用(第5节)。

blocks.en: 3.1 Setup
blocks.zh: 3.1 设置

blocks.en: Details on the setup, method, results, and prompts are in Appendix B and E .
blocks.zh: 关于设置、方法、结果和提示的细节见附录B和E。

blocks.en:
We build tasks from recorded sessions that meet three requirements.
First, the recording must show what the user wanted and how they reacted to the agent, so that an intent model can be built from it (e.g., contains real user messages and results of agent tool calls).
Second, a new agent must be able to redo the work from the starting environment alone (e.g., without external resources like GitHub pages or APIs).
Third, the user must have pushed back on at least one agent action, as the adaptation test builds on these actions.
Based on these requirements, we use 65 of the 109 sessions released by SWE-Together ( Wu et al., 2026b ) and 24 sessions from a newer release of SWE-chat ( Baumann et al., 2026 ) , for 89 tasks in all.
blocks.zh:
我们通过有记录的会议制定符合三项要求的任务。
首先,录制必须显示用户想要什么,以及他们对代理的反应,这样就可以从中构建一个意向模型(例如包含真正的用户消息和代理工具调用的结果).
第二,新代理必须能够独自从起始环境(如没有GitHub页面或API等外部资源)重做工作.
第三,由于适应测试是在这些行动的基础上进行的,用户必须至少推迟了一种代理人行动。
根据这些要求,我们使用SWE-Togleher(Wu等人,2026年b)发布的109场会议中的65场,以及SWE-chat(Baumann等人,2026年)最新发布的24场会议,总共完成89项任务。

blocks.en:
We compare SWE-WhatIf , with and without the style profile, against three other user simulators, all run on the same LLM (GPT-5.6 Luna).
For SWE-Together ( Wu et al., 2026b ) tasks, we use the simulator prompt released for each of its tasks, which lists the user’s later messages and in what conditions each one should be sent.
For the SWE-chat tasks, we use an LLM (Claude Opus 5.5) to write prompts in the same form.
This simulator also keeps a summary of each earlier agent turn. SWE-Interact ( Raghavendra et al., 2026 ) role-plays a terse colleague who reveals a list of requirements one at a time.
SWE-Interact derives this list from benchmark tasks (e.g., SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) ).
As our tasks come from recorded sessions, we use the intents and criteria from our intent model instead.
Finally, the goal-prompted simulator receives the same intents and criteria, but without a persona.
blocks.zh:
我们比较SWE-What 如果,与和没有样式配置,与另外三个用户模拟器,都运行在同一LLM(GPT-5.6 Luna)上.
对于SWE-Tother(Wu et al., 2026b)任务,我们使用为每项任务发布的模拟器即时,其中列出了用户的后期消息,以及每个用户的发送条件.
对于SWE聊天任务,我们使用LLM(英语:Claude Opus 5.5)来以同样形式写出提示.
这个模拟器还保存了每个较早的代理转折的摘要. SWE-Interact (Raghavendra等人, 2026年) 角色扮演一个三角同事,
SWE-Interact从基准任务(如SWE-bench(Jimenez等人,2024年))中得出这一清单.
由于我们的任务来自有记录的会议,我们改用我们的意图模式中的意图和标准。
最后,进球速成模拟器得到的意向和标准相同,但没有人称.

blocks.en: 3.2 Method
blocks.zh: 3.2 方法

blocks.en: Each test compares simulators on the same tasks.
blocks.zh: 每个测试都比较相同任务的模拟器.

blocks.en:
At every user reply in the recorded sessions, we give each simulator the conversation up to that reply and have it generate the next reply.
Simulators that keep a state across turns also receive the state built from the conversation so far (i.e., the intent states of SWE-WhatIf and summaries of earlier turns for SWE-Together).
An LLM judge (GPT-6.1 Sol) rates the similarity of each generated reply with the real user’s reply on content and style from 1 to 5, adapting the similarity ratings of SimulatorArena ( Dou et al., 2025 ) , and we scale the mean of the two ratings to 0–100.
In a replay, however, each reply builds on the simulator’s own earlier replies rather than the real user’s.
To test this, we also use a multi-turn setting, where each simulator writes three consecutive replies between the recorded agent turns, and the judge rates the three against the real user’s three replies.
blocks.zh:
在录制会话的每个用户回复时,我们都会给每个模拟器的对话直到该回复,并让其生成下一个回复.
保持一个状态横跨转弯的模拟器也接收了迄今为止从对话中构建的状态(即SWE-WhatIf的意向状态和SWE-Together之前转弯的概要).
LLM评委(GPT-6.1 Sol)将每个生成的回复的相似性与真实用户对内容和风格的回复从1到5, 将模拟Arena(Dou等人, 2025年)的相似性评分调整为0–100,
然而,在回放中,每个答复都基于模拟器自己先前的答复,而不是真正的用户的答复。
为了测试这一点,我们也使用一个多回合的设置,每个模拟器在录制的代理器之间连续写三次答复,法官根据真实用户的三次答复来评分这三项.

blocks.en:
We rewrite each recorded session by using an LLM to paraphrase all turns and merging some consecutive user turns.
We then run the same single-turn and multi-turn tests on the rewritten sessions, to check that a simulator does not rely on the exact wording and order of the recorded turns.
blocks.zh:
我们使用 LLM 重写每个录制的会话来解释所有转折, 并合并一些连续的用户转折 。
然后我们在重写的会话上进行同样的单转和多转的测试,以检查一个模拟器不依赖于所记录的转弯的准确措辞和顺序.

blocks.en:
For each task and user simulator, we replay the session with two agents (Claude Code on Claude Sonnet 5.5): one instructed to repeat the actions that the user pushed back on ( observed policy ) and one instructed to avoid them ( proactive policy ).
Following prior work ( Baumann et al., 2026 ; Tang et al., 2026b ; Tang et al., 2026a ) , we use an LLM (GPT-5.6 Terra) to identify these actions (e.g., ones that the user corrected, objected to, or reverted) and to write the instructions for each policy.
For each user simulator, we replay sessions with each agent policy twice.
We compare the burden-adjusted success (§ 2.4 ) of each proactive-policy replay with each observed-policy replay of the same task, and report the win rate of the proactive policy on a scale of 0 to 100, counting a tie as half a win ( Vargha and Delaney, 2000 ) .
We use two-sided sign tests to assess whether the proactive policy wins significantly more often than it loses, with Holm correction across the five simulators ( Holm, 1979 ) .
blocks.zh:
对于每个任务和用户模拟器,我们用两个代理(克劳德·索内5.5上的Claude Code)重播会话:一个指示重复用户退后的行动(遵守政策),一个指示避免(主动政策).
继先前的工作(Baumann等人,2026年;Tang等人,2026年b;Tang等人,2026年a)之后,我们使用LLM(GPT-5.6 Terra)来确定这些行动(例如,用户纠正、反对或恢复的行动),并为每项政策编写说明。
对于每个用户模拟器,我们用每个代理策略重播会话两次.
我们把每个主动政策重现的负担调整成功(§2.4)与每个观察到的政策重现相同的任务进行比较,并报告主动政策在0到100的尺度上的赢率,将平局算作半赢(Vargha和Delaney,2000年)。
我们用双面标志测试来评估主动政策是否胜过败,

blocks.en: 3.3 Results
blocks.zh: 3.3 结果

blocks.en:
Table 1 gives the results of the three tests, and Figure 3 plots each user simulator’s scores on the adaptation test against the average of its replication and robustness scores. SWE-WhatIf scored at least as high as SWE-Together on replication and robustness, while also being the simulator with which the proactive policy reached the highest win rate and won significantly more tasks than it lost.
Thus, SWE-WhatIf showed the most faithful adaptability among the simulators, replying as the real user did on the recorded sessions while still responding to a different agent as the user would.
blocks.zh:
表1列出了三次测试的结果,图3列出了每个用户模拟器在适应测试中的分数,并对照其复制和稳健性分数的平均值。 SWE-What如果得分至少相当于SWE-在复制和稳健性上的合作,同时也是主动政策达到最高赢率并赢得比失去的任务大得多的模拟器.
因此,SWE-What如果在模拟器中表现出最忠实的适应能力,就如同真实的用户在录制的会话中所做的那样回答,同时仍然像用户那样对不同的代理机做出响应.

blocks.en:
SWE-WhatIf scored highest on the recorded sessions, both for single replies (53.2, against 51.3 for SWE-Together) and for three consecutive replies (44.9 against 40.4), even though SWE-Together’s prompt provides the recorded user’s later messages verbatim.
In comparison, SWE-Interact and the goal-prompted simulator scored lower in both settings.
All simulators scored lower in the multi-turn setting than in single-turn.
blocks.zh:
SWE-What如果在录制的会话中得分最高,无论是单次回答(53.2,对SWE-Togleher51.3)还是连续三次回答(44.9对40.4),尽管SWE-Togle的提示提供了录制的用户后期消息的逐字记录.
相比之下,SWE-Interact和进球促销模拟器在两种设置中都得分较低.
所有模拟器在多回合设定中得分低于单回合.

blocks.en:
On the rewritten sessions, SWE-WhatIf and SWE-Together scored about the same (45.1 and 44.7 on average).
Both scored lower than on the recorded sessions, while SWE-Interact and the goal-prompted simulator were more robust to the paraphrased and merged turns, which can be expected as their replies are already more general and less tied to the content of the recording.
blocks.zh:
在重写会话中,SWE-What If和SWE-Toher的得分大致相同(平均为45.1和44.7).
两者的得分均低于录制的会话,而SWE-Interact和球速模拟器则对解码和合并的转折更为有力,这可以预期,因为他们的答复已经比较笼统,与录制内容的联系较少.

blocks.en:
SWE-WhatIf led to the highest win rate for the proactive policy (66.3), and removing the style profile lowered it to 62.9 (Table 1 ).
With the two versions of SWE-WhatIf , the proactive policy won 52 tasks and lost 23 with the style profile, and won 50 and lost 27 without.
blocks.zh:
SWE-What如果导致主动政策最高的赢率(66.3),取消风格描述将其降为62.9(表1)。
凭借SWE-What If的两个版本,主动政策赢得了52项任务,随着风格简介损失了23项,赢得了50项,没有赢得了27项.

blocks.en:
To understand when and why the user simulators did not distinguish the two policies in the adaptation test, we first inspected the simulated user turns in tasks where the replays tied or favored the observed policy, and identified four kinds of error in the simulator.
We then used an LLM (Claude Sonnet 5.5) to label the first replay with each policy in every task (Table 2 ).
As expected, the goal-prompted simulator tended to state all of its intents in its first turns, so the replays with both policies were similarly successful and took few turns.
SWE-Interact and SWE-WhatIf more often asked for extra work (e.g., pasting a diff, reviewing the changes, or running the checks again), which the real user never requested in the recorded session.
When the replayed agent departed from the recorded trajectory, SWE-Together had no scripted message that fit, so it mostly replied passively by accepting what the agent did or telling the agent to continue without steering the session.
blocks.zh:
为了理解用户模拟器在适应测试中何时和为什么没有区分两种政策,我们首先检查了模拟用户在重播绑定或偏爱所观察到的政策的任务中转弯,并确定了模拟器的四种错误.
然后我们用LLM(Claude Sonnet 5.5)来标注每个任务中的第一个重播策略(表2).
如所料,目标速成模拟器往往在最初的转折中阐述其所有意图,因此,与两项政策重演同样成功,转折很少。
SWE-Interact和SWE-What 如果更经常地要求额外工作(例如粘贴一个diff,审查修改,或再次运行检查),而真实的用户在录制的会话中从未要求额外工作.
当重播代理离开录制的轨迹时,SWE-Togle没有适合的脚本消息,因此它大多被动地回答,接受代理所做的,或者告诉代理在不引导会话的情况下继续.

blocks.en: 4 Evaluating LLMs as Coding Agents
blocks.zh: 4 评价作为编码代理人的有限责任公司

blocks.en:
We use SWE-WhatIf to rank LLMs as coding agents by how well they serve the users in the recorded sessions.
We replay 58 of the 65 tasks from SWE-Together’s sessions once with five LLMs (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, and Kimi K3) in the same agent harness, opencode ( Anomaly, 2025 ) —excluding seven tasks where an agent could not finish within the time limit.
We then rank the models by their mean burden-adjusted success over the tasks (§ 2.4 ).
Details are in Appendix B.5 .
blocks.zh:
我们使用 SWE-What 如果将LLMs 列为编码代理,
在SWE-Toher的65个任务中,我们用5个LLM(Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, 和Kimi K3)在同一个代理牵引装置中重播58个(Anomaly, 2025)——不包括一个代理无法在时限内完成的7个任务.
然后,我们按这些模型在任务上按平均负担调整的成功程度排列(第2.4节)。
详情见附录B.5。

blocks.en:
We compare our ranking with three published rankings that differ in user involvement: DeepSWE ( Huang et al., 2026 ) (i.e., no user), SWE-Together’s leaderboard ( Wu et al., 2026b ) (i.e., simulated users), and Agent Arena ( Chiang et al., 2024 ; Arena, 2026 ) (i.e., real users’ sessions with coding agents).
Our ranking agreed with Agent Arena’s more closely ( τ b \tau_{b} =.80) than SWE-Together’s ( τ b \tau_{b} =.60) and DeepSWE’s ( τ b \tau_{b} =.53) did (Figure 4 ), which suggests that it could more closely reflect how real users judge coding agents.
As seen in Appendix B.5 , Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 met about as many goals (65.3%, 65.1%), but the user required fewer messages with Opus (6.4 and 6.7 on average).

blocks.en:
To demonstrate how the best agent can differ between users or sessions, we group the tasks by two properties of their intent models and rank the agents within each group (Figure 4 ).
First, we group the tasks by whether they involve reactive intents (i.e., intents that the user raises only if a specific situation arises during the replay, like a test or a review that suggests another change).
We also split the tasks by whether their opening request is detailed (i.e., states more than two criteria of its intents; 26 tasks), or brief (32 tasks).
GPT-6 Sol ranked first on tasks without reactive intents and fourth on tasks with them.
This suggests that the Claude models better handle tasks where additional intents become relevant during the agent’s work, while GPT-6 Sol performs better when no intents depend on situations that arise during the replay.
With detailed requests, the models met similar numbers of goals and the GPT models needed fewer messages, while with brief requests the Claude models met more goals.
This suggests that the GPT models more efficiently complete tasks whose requirements are stated upfront, while the Claude models perform better when requirements are raised later.
blocks.zh:
为了证明最佳代理如何在用户或会话之间有所区别,我们按其意图模型的两个属性对任务进行分组,并对每个组中的代理进行排序(图4 ).
首先,我们按任务是否涉及被动意图(即只有在重播期间出现特定情况时用户才会提出的意向)来分类,比如一个测试或建议进行另一变化的审查.
我们还将任务分成两部分,一是详细提出开放请求(即说明其意图的两个以上标准;26项任务),二是简短(32项任务)。
GPT-6 Sol在没有反应意图的任务上排名第一,在与它们一起的任务上排名第四.
这表明克劳德模型在代理工作期间,如果额外的意向变得相关,则能更好地处理任务,而GPT-6 Sol则在意向不取决于重播期间出现的情况时能更好地执行.
在详细要求下,这些模型达到了类似数量的目标,而GPT模型需要的信息较少,而克劳德模型则在简短要求下实现了更多的目标.
这表明,GPT模式更有效率地完成预先说明其要求的任务,而克劳德模式在稍后提出要求时表现更好。

blocks.en: 5 User Study
blocks.zh: 5 用户研究

blocks.en:
SWE-WhatIf can allow users of coding agents to replay their own sessions with different agent harnesses and models, which could show them which agents best handle their tasks and steering patterns.
To understand what users learn from such replays, we conducted a study with 16 users of coding agents.
blocks.zh:
SWE-What 如果可以允许编码代理的用户用不同的代理吊带和模型重播自己的会话,这可以显示哪些代理最能处理他们的任务和引导模式.
为了了解用户从这种重播中学到了什么,我们与16个编码代理的用户进行了一项研究.

blocks.en:
We recruited participants through Prolific.
In our study interface, each participant provided one of their own recorded sessions, from which a SWE-WhatIf user simulator was built and used to replay part of the session with three agents for up to three turns each.
Before seeing the replays, participants first predicted how each agent would rank in the replays.
Then, they walked through the replays side by side where the agent used in each replay was hidden, and they then ranked the anonymous agents.
At the end, each replay’s agent was revealed and participants were asked what they learned from the replays and whether this would change how they use agents in the future.
Participants also rated how closely the simulated user’s replies represented how they steer agents and write messages.
Details in Appendix C .
blocks.zh:
我们通过Prolific招募了参与者。
在我们的研究界面中,每个参与者提供了他们自己录制的会话之一,从中建造了一个SWE-What 如果用户模拟器,并用来用三个代理重播会话的一部分,每个代理最多三个转弯.
在看到重播之前,参与者首先预言了每个经纪人在重播中会如何排位.
之后,他们通过复演并肩行走,在每次复演中使用的代理被隐藏的地方,然后对匿名代理进行排名.
最后,每一次重播的代理被揭发,参与者被问到他们从重播中学到了什么,这是否会改变他们未来使用代理的方式.
与会者也评价模拟用户的答复如何接近他们如何引导代理和写信息。
详情见附录C。

blocks.en: Figure 5: (a) Mean rank that participants gave each agent before reading the replays (start of each arrow) and after (arrowhead), where 1 is best. The number of participants who saw each agent is in parentheses. (b) Participants’ agreement with the four statements about their user simulators and the replays (16 participants).
blocks.zh: 图5:(a) 参与者在读取重播(每个箭头开始)和后面(箭头)前给每个代理人的均分排名,其中1是最优的。 见到每个代理人的参与者人数在括号内。 (b) 与会者同意关于用户模拟器和重播的四项声明(16名与会者)。

blocks.en:
After reading the replays, 14 of 16 participants ranked the agents differently from their initial prediction, and 10 changed which agent they ranked first.
On average, participants ranked the smaller model of each set higher than they had predicted, and Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol lower (Fig. 5 a).
Fifteen agreed that the replays taught them something they did not know about the agents, and 14 agreed that the replays would help them decide how to use coding agents (Fig. 5 b).
blocks.zh:
在读完重播后,16名参与者中有14名对代理的排名与其最初的预测不同,10名改变了他们排名第一的代理.
平均来说,参与者将每集中较小的模型排在比他们预测的要高的位置,克劳德·奥普斯·5.5和GPT-6 Sol则排在更低的位置(图5 a).
15人同意重播会教给他们一些他们不知道的关于特工的东西,14人同意重播会帮助他们决定如何使用编码代理(图5b).

blocks.en:
The most common lesson was that a smaller and cheaper model was enough for their session (12 of 16)—e.g., “Luna performed as well as Sol at a fraction of the cost.”
Participants also saw that agents differed in how they worked with the user, and this could affect which agent they preferred (8 of 16).
For example, P04 preferred an agent that “listened to what I had to say” over one that kept proposing its own ideas.
Also, 4 participants confirmed or revised their harness preferences (e.g., Claude Code or Codex), and 2 learned that their steering shapes the result.
For future use, 11 of 16 planned to choose models by task, including 5 who would start with a smaller model, 4 planned to change their steering, and 3 would keep their current harness.
blocks.zh:
最常见的教训是,一个较小和费用低廉的模型足以用于他们的会议(16个中的12个)——例如, " Luna和Sol的演出也只花费了一小部分费用。 “
与会者还看到,代理人在与使用者合作的方式上存在差异,这可能影响他们喜欢的代理人(16人中有8人)。
例如,P04倾向于一个“听从我不得不说的话”的代理人,而不是一个不断提出自己想法的代理人。
此外,有4名与会者确认或修订了他们的驾驭偏好(如Claude Code或Codex),有2名与会者了解到,他们的舵决定了这一结果。
供今后使用,16个中11个计划按任务选择模型,包括5个从较小的模型开始,4个计划改变方向,3个计划保留目前的操纵.

blocks.en:
Thirteen of 16 participants agreed that their simulated selves worded messages like them, and 13 agreed that they asked for things and reacted to the agent like them.
Participants marked 49% of the simulated replies as “Sounds like me”, 38% as “Partly”, and 13% as “Not like me”.
Where the simulated user differed, 5 participants found it more formal or wordier than themselves (e.g., P15: “with a lot more formality than I would”), and 3 found that it kept insisting on the same thing when they would not have (Appendix C ).
blocks.zh:
16名参与者中有13人同意他们模拟自己像他们这样用文字表达的信息,13人同意他们要求的东西,并对像他们这样的代理人作出反应.
与会者将模拟答复的49%标为“像我一样”,38%标为“部分”,13%标为“不像我”。
在模拟用户不同的地方,有5名参与者发现其形式比自己更正式或更文字(例如P15:“形式比我更正式”),有3名参与者发现,在他们不会这样做的时候,它仍然坚持同样的要求(附录C)。

blocks.en: 6 Related Work
blocks.zh: 6 相关工作

blocks.en:
Benchmarks for coding agents mainly assess fully specified tasks without a user ( Wang et al., 2026b ) , such as SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) and AppWorld ( Trivedi et al., 2024 ) .
As coding agents are increasingly used in practice, recent work adds simulated users to these benchmarks ( Pan et al., 2025 ; Kim et al., 2025a ; Trinh et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2024 ) who reveal requirements when asked ( Vijayvargiya et al., 2026 ) or one at a time ( Raghavendra et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh:
编码剂的基准主要是在没有用户的情况下评估完全指定的任务(Wang等人,2026b),例如SWE-bench(Jimenez等人,2024年)和AppWorld(Trivedi等人,2024年).
由于编码剂在实践中越来越多地被使用,最近的工作在这些基准中增加了模拟用户(Pan等人,2025年;Kim等人,2025年a;Trinh等人,2026年;Wang等人,2024年),他们被问及时会披露要求(Vijayvargiya等人,2026年)或一次披露要求(Raghavendra等人,2026年)。

blocks.en:
User simulation in task-oriented dialogue ( Schatzmann et al., 2006 ) includes agenda-based approaches ( Schatzmann et al., 2007 ) .
Recent work prompts LLMs with goals ( Yao et al., 2025 ; Barres et al., 2026 ; Wu et al., 2025 ) or personas ( Raghavendra et al., 2026 ) , or trains them to simulate users ( Zhou et al., 2026b ; Sun et al., 2026 ; Phan et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026a ) .
Further, simulators have also been designed to model specific user behaviors, such as progressive disclosure ( Laban et al., 2026 ) , evolving intents ( Kim et al., 2026 ; Tack et al., 2026 ) , contextual preferences ( Kim et al., 2025b ) , knowledge ( Lee et al., 2026 ) , and cooperation ( Chopra et al., 2026 ) .
Others build simulators from real user data ( Wu et al., 2026a ; Naous et al., 2026 ) , including inferred profiles ( Wang et al., 2025 ; Zhou et al., 2026a ) , but simulated users can still differ from real users in their interaction behavior and failure patterns ( Zhou et al., 2026c ; Seshadri et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh:
面向任务的对话中的用户模拟(Schatzmann等人,2006年)包括基于议程的方法(Schatzmann等人,2007年)。
最近的工作激励了具有目标的有限责任公司(姚等人,2025年;Barres等人,2026年;Wu等人,2025年)或permanas(Raghavendra等人,2026年),或培训他们模拟用户(周等人,2026年b; Sun等人,2026年;Phan等人,2026年;Wang等人,2026年a).
此外,还设计了模拟器,以模拟特定用户的行为,例如渐进披露(Laban等人,2026年),不断发展的意图。 (Kim等人,2026年;Tack等人,2026年),背景偏好 (Kim等人,2025b),知识(Lee等人,2026),合作(Chopra等人,2026).
其他人根据真实用户数据构建模拟器(Wu等人,2026a;Naous等人,2026),包括推断的剖面图(Wang等人,2025;Zhou等人,2026a),但模拟用户在互动行为和故障模式上仍可与真实用户有所区别(Wu等人,2026c;Seshadri等人,2026).

blocks.en:
Recorded coding-agent sessions ( Baumann et al., 2026 ; DataClaw contributors, 2026 ; He et al., 2026 ) support analyses of user steering ( Tang et al., 2026b ; Tang et al., 2026a ) and evaluation on real tasks.
SWE-Together ( Wu et al., 2026b ) replays these sessions by deciding when to send the recorded user’s messages, while preserving their content and order.
Instead, SWE-WhatIf generates replies from the user’s intents, criteria, and conditions, allowing it to respond to new agent trajectories.
blocks.zh:
录音编码代理会(Baumann等人,2026年;DataClaw撰稿人,2026年;He等人,2026年)支持用户引导分析(Tang等人,2026年b;Tang等人,2026年a)以及对实际任务的评价.
SWE-Tother(Wu et al., 2026b)通过决定何时发送已录制的用户消息,同时保留其内容和秩序来重播这些会话.
相反,SWE-What如果从用户的意图、标准和条件中生成回复,则使其能够对新的代理轨迹作出反应。

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
We introduce SWE-WhatIf , a framework for replaying recorded user–agent sessions with new coding agents by simulating users from their intents, criteria, and conditions.
In tests of replication and robustness, SWE-WhatIf generated the replies most similar to those of real users on recorded sessions and matched the strongest baseline when sessions were rewritten.
In an adaptation test, our simulator most clearly distinguished agents that avoided actions that the real users had objected to from those that repeated them.
By ranking five LLMs as coding agents and through a user study where participants replayed their own sessions, we demonstrate that replays can help researchers evaluate agents on real users’ work and help developers choose agents for their own tasks.
blocks.zh:
SWE-What If 是一个通过模拟用户的意图、标准和条件来与新编码代理重播记录的用户代理会话的框架。
在复制和稳健性的测试中,SWE-What如果生成的答复与所记录的会话中真实用户的答复最相似,并匹配重写会话时最强的基准.
在一次适应测试中,我们的模拟器最明显地区别于避免了真实用户反对的行为和重复的行为.
通过将5个LLMs列为编码代理商,并通过参与者重播他们自己的会话的用户研究,我们证明重播可以帮助研究人员评价真正的用户工作的代理商,并帮助开发商为自己的任务选择代理商.

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
Our replays make the following assumptions about users.
First, the user interacts with the agent only through the conversation.
In practice, users may also open and edit files, run tests on their own, or look at external resources, but these are not shown in the recorded session.
Second, the user implicitly accepted any outcome they did not object to, which ignores cases where the user might have been dissatisfied but did not express it.
Third, the simulated user does not react to anything for which the recorded session has no relevant evidence (e.g., if a new agent adds comments to the code but the user never reacted to code comments in the recorded session, the simulated user ignores them).
Similarly, the simulated user only asks for what the user asked for in the recording, even when a new agent’s path might have led the real user to new requests.
Finally, the simulated user reads every tool call and its result, while a real user may only skim the agent’s work.
We leave relaxing these assumptions for future work.
blocks.zh:
我们的重播对用户做了以下假设.
首先,用户只能通过对话与代理进行互动.
在实践中,用户也可以打开和编辑文件,自行进行测试,或者查看外部资源,但这些内容没有在录制的会话中显示.
其次,用户默认接受他们不反对的任何结果,这忽略了用户可能不满意但没有表达出来的情况.
第三,模拟用户不会对所记录的会话没有相关证据的任何东西作出反应(例如,如果新代理在代码中添加评论,但用户在所记录的会话中从未对代码评论作出反应,则模拟用户会忽略它们).
同样,模拟用户只问用户在录音中要求什么,即使新代理的路径可能已经使真正的用户接到新的请求.
最后,模拟用户读取每个工具调用及其结果,而真正的用户可能只滑动代理的作品.
我们为今后的工作而放松这些假设。

blocks.en:
Our experiments also have the following limitations.
The used sessions come from public releases, so they include only developers who chose to publish their sessions (e.g., SWE-chat ( Baumann et al., 2026 ) mostly includes early adopters working on open-source code, not on proprietary or enterprise code).
For agent evaluation and ranking, we evaluated only five models in a single agent harness, opencode ( Anomaly, 2025 ) .
Our metric for burden-adjusted success approximates the user’s effort of writing and reading by counting messages, and the goals used to measure success are based on where the recorded session ended, but the user may have stopped midway instead of reaching the state they wanted.
In the user study, participants saw only three agents that we chose, for up to three turns each, and these agents worked in environments partially reconstructed from the recording, which may not reflect their full capabilities.
blocks.zh:
我们的实验也有以下局限性.
所使用的会话来自公开发布,因此它们只包括选择发布会话的开发者(如SWE-chat(Baumann等人,2026年)),大多包括早期从事开源代码工作的采纳者,而不是专有代码或企业代码.
就代理评价和排名而言,我们只评价了单一代理带中的五个模型,即Opencode(Anomaly,2025年)。
我们衡量负重调整成功与否的尺度, 大致相当于用户通过计数信件来写作和阅读的努力, 衡量成功与否的目标,
在用户研究中,参与者只看到我们选择的3个代理,每个代理最多3个转弯,这些代理在从录音中部分重建的环境中工作,这可能不能反映他们的全部能力.

blocks.en: Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en:
Our experiments use recorded sessions released publicly by SWE-Together ( Wu et al., 2026b ) and SWE-chat ( Baumann et al., 2026 ) .
SWE-Together is released under the Apache 2.0 license, with sessions originally collected from SWE-chat (ODC-By), DataClaw (MIT), Pi, and Hyperswitch.
We use these sessions to evaluate coding agents and user simulators, consistent with the purposes of these releases.
However, recorded sessions can contain sensitive information, such as private code, credentials, and identifying details.
Building user simulators from these sessions can further expose this information through their intent models, style profiles, and simulated replays.
blocks.zh:
我们的实验使用SWE-Together(Wu等人,2026年b)和SWE-chat(Baumann等人,2026年b)公开发布的记录会.
SWE-Together根据Apache 2.0许可发布,会话最初收集自SWE-chat(ODC-By),DataClaw(MIT),Pi,以及Hyperswitch.
我们利用这些会话来评价编码代理和用户模拟器,这符合这些发布的目的.
然而,所记录的会议可以包含敏感信息,如私人代码、全权证书和识别细节。
从这些会话中构建用户模拟器,可以通过其意向模型,样式配置和模拟重播进一步曝光这些信息.

blocks.en:
In our user study, participants gave informed consent before providing their sessions.
Before uploading, we replaced credentials and identifying details on participants’ own computers and sent only the portions of sessions needed for the replays.
Participants were informed that their sessions would be sent to the model providers that ran the agents and user simulator.
After generating the replays, we deleted the uploaded sessions, intent models, style profiles, and starting environments.
We do not release an artifact package containing the source sessions, code, intent models, style profiles, goals, or simulated replays.
The study was approved by KAIST’s institutional review board.
blocks.zh:
在我们的用户研究中,与会者在提供会议之前给予了知情同意。
在上传之前,我们更换了全权证书,在与会者自己的电脑上找出细节,只发送了复播所需的会议部分。
与会者被告知,他们的会议将发给运营代理商和用户模拟器的模型提供者。
生成重播后,我们删除了上传的会话,意向模型,样式配置,以及起始环境.
我们不发布包含源会话,代码,意图模型,风格简介,目标,或模拟重播的文物包.
这项研究得到KAIST机构审查委员会的批准。

blocks.en:
Beyond privacy, SWE-WhatIf raises another concern because it simulates how a particular user communicates with and steers coding agents.
Although we use these simulators only to evaluate coding agents, they could also be used to imitate the real users in other settings without their knowledge or consent.
This risk is especially relevant when sharing intent models, style profiles, or simulated replays that capture how a particular user behaves.
blocks.zh:
除了隐私之外,SWE-What 如果引起另一个关注,因为它模拟了特定用户如何与编码代理进行沟通和引导.
虽然我们使用这些模拟器只是为了评价编码代理,但它们也可以被用来在其他场合模仿真正的用户,而无需他们知情或同意.
在分享意图模型,样式配置,或模拟重播,捕捉特定用户的行为方式时,这种风险尤其相关.

blocks.en:
We used AI assistants to help implement the user simulator, build the user study interface, revise the manuscript, and search the literature.
The authors verified and revised all resulting content and read the cited papers.
blocks.zh:
我们利用AI助手帮助实施用户模拟器,构建用户学习界面,修改手稿,搜索文献.
提交人核实并修订了所有由此产生的内容,并阅读了上述文件。

blocks.en: Appendix A User Simulator Details
blocks.zh: 附录 A 用户模拟器细节

blocks.en: Here, we provide the details of how SWE-WhatIf builds the intent model of each task and how the user simulator replies after each agent turn.
blocks.zh: 在此,我们详细介绍SWE-What 如果建立每项任务的意向模型,以及用户模拟器在每个代理商转身后如何回复.

blocks.en: A.1 Building the Intent Model
blocks.zh: A.1 建立意向模式

blocks.en: We build each intent model with three LLM-based agents that draft, review, and revise it in turn, all Claude Code on Claude Opus 5.5.
blocks.zh: 我们用三个基于LLM的代理人 来构建每一个意图模型 依次起草、审查和修订 克劳德·奥普斯5.5上的克劳德代码

blocks.en: Each agent takes the recorded session (i.e., every message of the user and the agent, and the results of the agent’s tool calls) and also the starting environment (i.e., the code repository with its history and its runtime).
blocks.zh: 每个代理都负责录制的会话(即用户和代理的每条消息,以及代理工具调用的结果)以及起始环境(即代码寄存器及其历史和运行时间).

blocks.en: The drafting agent writes the intent model through five steps (prompt in Fig. 14 , with the rules in Fig. 17 ): (1) label what each user message does (e.g., a request, a correction, or an acceptance of the agent’s work); (2) group messages into intents and write the criteria of each intent; (3) for each criterion, record the evidence in the session and what the simulated user could observe in a replay to judge it; (4) write the conditions; and (5) mark where in each session each criterion and condition was met.
blocks.zh: 起草人员通过五个步骤(图14中的提示,图17中的规则)来写意向模型:(1)将每个用户信息所做的事情(如请求,更正,或接受代理的工作)标注在标签上;(2)将集体信息写成意向,并写出每个意向的标准;(3)针对每个标准,在会话中记录证据以及模拟用户在重播中可以观察到什么来判断它;(4)写条件;(5)标注每个会话中是否符合每个标准和条件.

blocks.en:
We instruct the drafting agent to follow specific rules that tie the intent model to the user’s own requests and decisions.
The following are the main rules that are followed: • An intent or criterion should refer to names that were only named explicitly by the user, given in the opening request, or already held by the starting environment. • A criterion can require a specific approach to code changes only if the user requested that approach explicitly or they explicitly accepted when an agent took that approach. Otherwise, the criterion must be described so that it can be satisfied by other equivalent approaches. • A condition records what led the user to raise an intent in the conversation. • A question and the request that follows its answer are two intents, where the second has a condition that depends on the first. • If new information leads the user to replace one request with another, represent the original and replacement requests as separate intents.
Give the original intent a condition that drops it when that information appears in the replay.
If the user instead refines what they want from the same outcome, without learning new information, keep one intent and write its criteria to reflect the user’s final requirements.
blocks.zh:
我们指示起草人遵循具体规则,将意图模式与用户自己的要求和决定联系起来。
遵循的主要规则如下: 意图或标准应当指名称仅由用户明确命名、在开口请求中给出或由起始环境已经持有。 • 支助 一项标准只有在用户明确要求采用该方法或在代理人采取该方法时明确接受该方法的情况下,才能要求对代码进行具体修改。 否则,必须描述这一标准,以便用其他类似办法满足。 • 支助 一个条件记录了导致用户在谈话中提出意图的原因. • 支助 问题和答案后面的要求是两个意图,第二个意图的条件取决于第一个意图。 如果新信息导致用户将一个请求替换为另一个请求,则代表原始请求和替换请求作为单独的意图.
给原意图一个条件,当信息出现在重播中时,它会放弃它.
如果用户在不学习新信息的情况下,改进他们从相同结果中想要的东西,则保留一种意图,并写出反映用户最后要求的标准。

如果新信息导致用户将一个请求替换为另一个请求,则代表原始请求和替换请求作为单独的意图.
给原意图一个条件,当信息出现在重播中时,它会放弃它.
如果用户在不学习新信息的情况下,改进他们从相同结果中想要的东西,则保留一种意图,并写出反映用户最后要求的标准。

blocks.en:
The reviewing agent reads the session, the draft, and the starting environment, and lists issues without changing the draft (Fig. 15 ).
While reviewing, it can also run commands in the starting environment.
Finally, a revising agent fixes each listed issue (Fig. 16 ).
blocks.zh:
审查人员阅读会议、草案和起始环境,并列出问题,而不修改草案(图15)。
在审查的同时,它也可以在起始环境中运行命令.
最后,修订代理人将每个所列问题固定下来(图16)。

blocks.en: A.2 Simulating a Turn
blocks.zh: A.2 模拟转动

blocks.en:
Our user simulator runs on GPT-5.6 Luna at medium reasoning effort.
The simulator takes as input only the conversation of the replay, which includes the agent’s tool calls and their results.
blocks.zh:
我们的用户模拟器运行在GPT-5.6 Luna上 中度推理努力.
模拟器只将重播的对话作为输入,其中包含代理工具的调用及其结果.

blocks.en:
There are two types of conditions: a condition that depends on another intent (e.g., I1 satisfied) is checked by the simulator from the intent state, and a condition on a situation in the session or on information from the agent is written in text and judged by an LLM.
After each agent turn, an LLM judges the criteria of every raised or dropped intent, and every condition written in text, including those already met (Fig. 18 ).
For each judged criterion or condition, the LLM also describes its reasoning for its judgement.
blocks.zh:
有两种条件:一个条件取决于另一个意图(例如I1满足),由模拟器从意向状态检查,一个条件取决于会话中的某个情况或代理人提供的信息,由文字写成,由LLM判断.
在每个代理人转身后,一个LLM会判断每个提出或放弃意图的标准,以及用文字写成的每个条件,包括已经满足的条件(图18)。
对于每一项判断的标准或条件,LLM也描述了判断的理由.

blocks.en:
The simulator then updates the intent state from the judgments, without an LLM.
At the start of a replay, the intents in the opening request are raised, the intents without a raising condition are open, and all other intents are blocked.
A blocked intent becomes open when its raising conditions are met, and an open intent becomes raised only when the respond step expresses it.
An intent becomes dropped when its dropping conditions are met, and satisfied when all of its criteria are met.
Once a condition is met, it stays met.
In contrast, a met criterion becomes unmet again if a later agent turn does work that undoes or conflicts with the criterion.
A raised intent that is not satisfied is abandoned when none of its criteria change for four consecutive agent turns.
Blocked intents that depend on an abandoned intent are also abandoned.
A dropped or abandoned intent is never raised again.
blocks.zh:
然后模拟器从判决中更新意向状态,没有LLM.
重播开始时,开启请求中的意向被提出,没有提升条件的意向被打开,其他意向被屏蔽.
封锁的意图在满足提高条件时才开放,而开放的意图只有在反应步骤表达时才开放。
一旦满足了下降条件,就放弃了意图;如果满足了所有标准,就满足了意图。
一旦满足一个条件,它就继续满足.
与此相反,如果后一个代理人转身工作推翻或与该标准发生冲突,满足的标准就会再次得不到满足。
如果连续四个代理人转身时其标准没有改变,则未满足的上升意图即告放弃。
依赖于废弃意图的封禁意图也被废弃.
放弃或放弃的意向从此不再提出。

blocks.en:
An LLM then chooses which intents to express among those that are open or already raised but with unmet criteria (Fig. 19 ).
The LLM first writes what the reply should ask the agent to do, and then rewrites the reply to follow the user’s style with the style profile.
The respond step is also given the assess step’s reasoning for the judgement of each unmet criterion, so the simulator can name what is missing (e.g., the agent built the binary but never ran it).
blocks.zh:
然后,LLM选择在那些开放或已经提出但尚未达到标准的国家中表达哪些意图(图19)。
LLM首先写下答复应该请代理做什么,然后用样式配置重写回复,以遵循用户的风格.
回应步骤也被赋予了评估步骤对每个未达到标准判断的推理,因此模拟器可以点出所缺少的东西(例如,代理制造二进制但从未运行).

blocks.en:
We compute the style profile from the messages that the user typed in the recorded session with deterministic code.
These messages include the opening request and leave out slash commands and pasted text (i.e., messages longer than 600 characters or with six or more lines).
The style profile covers the language used, whether the first letter is capitalized, the end punctuation, the use of backticks, the length in words, and the use of specific words (e.g., “please”, “pls”, “thanks”).
For each pattern except length, the code counts the share of messages with the pattern and turns it into a fixed sentence (e.g., “None of their messages say please or thanks.”).
For length, the code takes the median number of words per message and places it in one of four classes, which are a few words (up to 6), one sentence (up to 15), one to three sentences (up to 35), and several sentences.
blocks.zh:
我们从用户在录制的会话中输入的信件中, 以决定性代码计算样式描述文件 。
这些消息包括打开请求,并留下斜线命令和粘贴文本(即超过600个字符或有6行或6行以上的消息).
风格简介涵盖所使用的语言,是否将第一个字母资本化,端点标出,使用回击,用词长度,以及使用特定单词(例如“请”、“pls”、“thanks”).
对于除长度外的每一种图案,代码会用图案来计算信件的份量,并将其变为固定句子(例如,“他们的任何信件都不要说请或感谢”。
对于长度,代码取每条消息的中位数,并放在四个类中的一个,即几个词(最多6个),一个句子(最多15个),一个到三个句子(最多35个),以及几个句子.

blocks.en:
A replay ends when every intent is satisfied, dropped, or abandoned, or when no intent changes for seven consecutive agent turns.
Intents that the user would want only if a situation arose (e.g., a test failing) are left out of this check while they are blocked.
blocks.zh:
重播在满足、放弃或放弃每一种意图时结束,或者在连续7个代理的意向没有改变时结束。
只有在出现某种情况(如测试失败)被屏蔽时,用户才会想要的意向才会被排除在此检查之外.

blocks.en: A.3 Example
blocks.zh: A.3 实例

blocks.en:
Figure 6 shows the intent model of one task and an excerpt of one of its replays.
In the recorded session, the user asks for a small patch to the command-line tool of a Go repository, so that the command entire explain prints its help text when it receives an argument without any of its qualifier flags (i.e., the flags that name what to explain).
When the recorded agent starts to edit the code, the user rejects the edit and asks it to create a branch first.
After the patch, the user runs /reviewer (i.e., a command defined in the repository that has the agent start a separate agent to review the changes).
The review approves the patch and suggests a hint that explains why the help text is shown, and the user asks for the hint if it is small.
The intent model keeps these requests as four intents. I2 has no raising condition, so it is open from the start of a replay. I3 is raised when I1 is satisfied, and I4 is raised only if a review suggests the hint ( C1 ).
blocks.zh:
图6显示一项任务的意向模型和其中一项重播的节选.
在录制的会话中,用户向Go寄存器的命令行工具请求一个小补丁,这样,当它收到一个没有任何限定标记的参数(即命名什么解释的旗帜)时,命令整个解释它的帮助文本.
当录制的代理开始编辑代码时,用户拒绝编辑,要求它先创建分支.
补丁后,用户运行/审查器(即寄存器中定义的让代理启动单独代理来审查更改的命令).
审查批准补丁,并提出提示,说明为何显示帮助文本,用户询问提示是否小.
意向模型将这些请求保留为四个意向. I2没有提升条件,因此从重播开始就开放. I3在I1满足时才会提出,而I4只有在审查提示(C1)时才会提出.

blocks.en:
In the excerpt, the new agent (Claude Code on Claude Sonnet 5.5) makes the patch, but its check also prints the help text when a qualifier flag is given.
As criterion (b) of I1 is unmet, the simulated user asks for this missing part.
In the third turn, the agent is unable to run /reviewer , as it has no tool to start another agent, which is a situation that was not present in the recording.
Then, the simulated user instead asks it to review the changes itself so the agent provides a review that approves the patch without suggesting a hint.
As a result, C1 is never met and the simulated user never asks for the hint.
The replay ended after five agent turns, with I1 to I3 satisfied.
In another replay with the same agent, the agent also does the same review but it instead suggested including a message that explains the help text.
This led the simulated user to ask for the hint in its next reply.
blocks.zh:
在节录中,新代理(Claude Code on Claude Sonnet 5.5)制作补丁,但它的检查在给定限定旗时也会打印帮助文本.
由于I1中的标准(b)没有得到满足,模拟用户要求得到这个缺失的部分.
在第三个回合,代理无法运行/审查器,因为它没有启动另一个代理的工具,这种情况在录音中并不存在.
然后,模拟用户要求它审查修改本身,这样代理提供审核,批准补丁而不提示.
因此,C1从未满足,模拟用户也从未要求提示.
重播在5个代理回合后结束,I1到I3满意.
在与同一代理商的另一项重播中,代理商也进行同样的审查,但建议包括一个解释帮助文本的信息.
这导致模拟用户在下次回复中询问提示.

blocks.en: Appendix B Experiment Details
blocks.zh: 附录B 实验细节

blocks.en: This appendix gives the details on the validation experiments for the user simulators (Section 3 ) and of the evaluation of LLMs as coding agents (Section 4 ).
blocks.zh: 本附录详细介绍了用户模拟器的验证试验(第3节)和对作为编码剂的LLMs的评价(第4节)。

blocks.en: B.1 Tasks
blocks.zh: B.1 任务

blocks.en:
We build our tasks from the 109 sessions released by SWE-Together ( Wu et al., 2026b ) , each with a prebuilt starting environment.
SWE-Together’s sessions were originally collected in an earlier release of SWE-chat ( Baumann et al., 2026 ) , DataClaw ( DataClaw contributors, 2026 ) , Pi ( Zechner, 2026 ) , and Hyperswitch ( Archit11, 2025 ) .
The release is under the Apache 2.0 license and states no separate license for its data.
The 89 tasks included the following languages: Chinese in 4 sessions, Vietnamese in 3 sessions, and English in the other 82.
blocks.zh:
我们从SWE-Togleher(Wu et al., 2026b)发布的109场会中构建我们的任务,每场会都有一个预建的起始环境.
SWE-Tother的会话最初是在较早的一次SWE-chat(Baumann等人,2026年)的发行中收集的. DataClaw. (DataClaw撰稿人,2026年),Pi(Zechner,2026年),和Hyperswitch(Archit11,2025年).
发布时使用Apache 2.0许可证,并声明其数据没有单独的许可证.
这89项任务包括下列语文: 中文分4届,越南语分3届,英文分其他82届.

blocks.en: Table 4: Identifiers of the 89 sessions that our tasks are built from. SWE-Together’s tasks are named by their task_id in its release, and SWE-chat’s sessions by their session_id in revision 202b071 of its release.
blocks.zh: 表4:确定我们的任务来自的89届会议。 SWE-Toher的任务由他们的任务命名,

blocks.en:
To increase the number of tasks, we also select sessions from a newer release of SWE-chat that SWE-Together does not include.
We first apply the same filters as SWE-Together (e.g., a repository with at least 10 stars, at least 30% of the code written by the agent), including its LLM-based check that a new agent can redo the work from the starting environment alone.
We then keep only sessions recorded with Claude Code or Codex that contain at least three messages from the user.
The starting commit of each session must also be recoverable from a public GitHub repository.
We exclude projects that would need a large amount of disk space to build (e.g., an Android SDK or Dart).
We also exclude sessions where the recorded agent relied on anything that is not available within the starting environment and requires external resources that may not be available during simulation (e.g., a GitHub issue or a tool that runs outside the repository).
Finally, as SWE-chat can include multiple sessions that come from the same repository, we increase diversity by selecting at most 8 sessions from each repository.
We create our own starting environments for each session that contains the repository at its starting commit and the runtime it needs.
blocks.zh:
为了增加任务数量,我们还从SWE-Tother不包含的SWE-chat的更新发布中选择会话.
我们首先应用与SWE-Together相同的滤波器(例如,一个拥有至少10颗恒星的寄存器,至少30%的代码由代理编写),包括它基于LLM的检查,即新代理可以独自从起始环境重做工作.
然后,我们只保留 Claude Code 或 Codex 记录的会话,其中包含用户至少3条消息.
每一会话的起始承诺也必须从一个公共的GitHub存储器中收回。
我们排除了需要大量磁盘空间来构建的项目(例如Android SDK或Dart).
我们还排除了被记录的代理依赖于初始环境中不存在的,并且需要模拟期间可能无法获得的外部资源(例如GitHub问题或运行在寄存器外的工具)的会话.
最后,由于SWE聊天可以包括来自同一寄存器的多个会话,我们通过在每个寄存器中最多从8个会话中选择来增加多样性.
我们为每场会议创造自己的起始环境,其中包含存储器的起始承诺和运行时间。

blocks.en:
In four of the 89 tasks, the session needs content outside of the starting environment (e.g., GitHub pages, external API) only in its first turns.
We start these tasks from a later user message that does not depend on that content.
The agent and the user simulator receive the earlier turns as conversation history.
blocks.zh:
在89项任务中的4项中,会话仅在首转时需要初始环境以外的内容(如GitHub页面,外部API).
我们从一个不依赖于该内容的后期用户消息开始这些任务.
代理和用户模拟器作为对话历史接收较早的转折.

blocks.en: B.2 User Simulators
blocks.zh: B.2 用户模拟器

blocks.en: All user simulators run on the same LLM (GPT-5.6 Luna) and write one reply after each agent turn.
blocks.zh: 所有用户模拟器运行在相同的LLM(GPT-5.6 Luna)上,在每个代理转弯后写一个回复.

blocks.en:
We use the simulator prompt that their released code provides for each task.
Some of our tasks exclude turns of the recorded session (e.g., the turns before the user message that a task starts from), but the provided prompt still describes them.
We remove these passages from the simulator prompt with an LLM (GPT-5.6 Terra).
For the SWE-chat tasks, which have no provided prompt, we use an LLM (Claude Opus 5.5) to write a prompt for each task in the form of the released prompts.
blocks.zh:
我们使用模拟器的提示,它们发布的代码为每一项任务提供了条件.
我们的一些任务排除了录制的会话的转折(例如,一个任务从用户消息开始之前的转折),但提供的提示仍然描述了它们.
我们用LLM(GPT-5.6 Terra)从模拟器的提示中去掉这些段落.
对于SWE聊天任务(SWE-chat),没有提供即时信息,我们使用LLM(Claude Opus 5.5)以发布即时信息的形式为每项任务写出即时信息.

blocks.en:
In SWE-Interact, the simulated user runs in fixed stages (i.e., a set order in which it reveals requirements derived from benchmark tasks) and it is able to inspect the repository or environment through tool calls.
We take their prompt, but with the intents and criteria of our intent model in place of the benchmark requirements (Fig. 20 ).
Additionally, for a fair comparison with the other simulators, we prevent the simulator from using tool calls to inspect its repository and environment.
The goal-prompted simulator receives the same intents and criteria from our intent model with a plain instruction to reply as the user (Fig. 21 ).
blocks.zh:
在SWE-Interact中,模拟用户以固定的阶段运行(即显示来自基准任务的要求的设定顺序),并且能够通过工具调用来检查寄存器或环境.
我们迅速采取行动,但我们的意图模式的意图和标准取代了基准要求(图20)。
此外,为了与其他模拟器进行公平比较,我们防止模拟器使用工具呼叫来检查其存储器和环境。
目标提示模拟器从我们的意向模型中得到了与用户相同的意向和标准,并有简单的回答指令(图21).

blocks.en: B.3 Method
blocks.zh: B.3 方法

blocks.en: This section gives the details of each test in Section 3.2 .
blocks.zh: 本节提供第3.2节中每项试验的细节。

blocks.en:
The LLM judge used to assess similarity of real user replies and simulated ones uses one prompt for single-turn replies and another one for the multi-turn setting (Figs. 22 and 23 ).
When we run the judge, we run it twice, average the two ratings, and rescale each rating to 0–100 as 100 ​ ( r − 1 ) / 4 100(r-1)/4 .
The recorded sessions of the 89 tasks contain 569 user replies that we used for evaluation.
At each reply, SWE-WhatIf starts from the intent state built from the conversation before the last agent turn, then assesses that turn, updates the intent state, and writes the reply.
For the multi-turn setting, we average the sets of three consecutive replies within each task, then average over the tasks that have at least one such set, which results in 71 tasks.
blocks.zh:
LLM法官用来评估真实用户答复的相似性,模拟用户答复使用一个单回合答复的速率,另一个用于多回合设置(图22和图23)。
当我们运行评委时,我们运行了两次,平均两个评分,并将每个评分调整为0–100为100(r–1)/4100(r-1)/4.
89项任务的录制会议载有569个用户的答复,我们用来进行评价。
在每次回复中, SWE-What如果从上次代理回合前的对话所形成的意向状态开始, 然后评估转弯, 更新意向状态, 并写下答复 。
关于多回合制,我们平均在每个任务中连续回答三个问题,然后平均回答至少有一个这样的一组任务,这导致71个任务。

blocks.en:
We rewrite a session in two ways, merging consecutive user turns and paraphrasing messages.
For merging, we ask an LLM (GPT-5.6 Luna) whether each pair of consecutive user turns could have been sent as one message (Fig. 25 ).
For such identified turns, we use an LLM to merge the turns with a short connecting phrase (e.g., “Also,”), which gives 153 merged turns over 72 tasks (Fig. 26 ).
For paraphrasing, we use the LLM to paraphrase each user and agent message (Fig. 24 ).
Then, for evaluation, we compare the simulated replies against the paraphrased versions of the real users’ replies.
blocks.zh:
我们以两种方式重写一个会话,合并连续的用户转弯和解析消息.
关于合并,我们询问一个LLM(GPT-5.6 Luna),每对连续的用户转弯是否可以作为一个消息发送(图25).
对于这种已识别的转弯,我们使用LLM将转弯与一个短的连接短语(如“Also,”)合并,使153个合并转弯超过72个任务(图26)。
对于参数,我们使用LLM来解释每个用户和代理消息(图24).
然后,为了评价,我们比较模拟答复与实际用户答复的简化版本。

blocks.en:
We use an LLM (GPT-5.6 Terra) to write the goals of each task from the recorded session alone, without the intent model (Fig. 27 ).
Each goal cites the user’s messages that support it, and work that the recorded agent did on its own is left out.
blocks.zh:
我们使用LLM(GPT-5.6 Terra)来单独从录制的会话中写出每项任务的目标,而没有意图模型(图27).
每个目标都引用了用户支持它的信息,而被录制的代理人自己完成的工作被排除在外.

blocks.en:
We use an LLM (GPT-5.6 Terra) to list, from the recorded session and its goals, every agent action that the user pushed back on (Fig. 28 ).
We then use the same LLM to turn each action in this list into an observed instruction that repeats it in similar situations and a proactive instruction that avoids it (Fig. 29 ).
For example, consider an agent that was corrected for committing all staged changes before asking the user which ones to commit.
The observed instruction will tell the agent to always commit all staged changes, while its proactive counterpart would tell the agent to inspect staged changes first and confirm with the user which ones to commit.
blocks.zh:
我们用LLM(GPT-5.6 Terra)从录制的会话和目标中列出用户推后的每一代理动作(图28)。

blocks.en:
To score task success, an LLM judge (GPT-6.1 Sol) reads the goals, the changes that the replay made to the repository, and the agent’s messages and tool calls (Fig. 30 ).
The judge does not read the messages of the real or simulated user, so that it judges each replay on the agent’s work alone.
We run the judge twice on each replay.
Success s s is the percentage of goals met, averaged over the two runs of the judge, and burden-adjusted success follows Section 2.4 .
For the win rate, we compare each proactive-policy replay of a task with each of its observed-policy replays, counting a win as 1, a tie as 0.5, and a loss as 0, and average the four comparisons into the task’s score ( Vargha and Delaney, 2000 ) .
The win rate is the mean of these scores over tasks.
We test whether the proactive policy wins more tasks than it loses with a two-sided sign test, which leaves out tasks with a score of exactly 0.5, and apply a Holm correction across the five user simulators ( Holm, 1979 ) .
blocks.zh:
为了评分任务的成功,一名LLM评委(GPT-6.1 Sol)阅读了目标,重播对寄存器的更改,以及代理商的信息和工具呼叫(图30).
法官不阅读真实用户或模拟用户的讯息,因此,法官判断每个用户只重播经纪人的工作。
每次重播时我们都要主持两次评委
成功是达到的目标的百分比,平均在法官的两次竞选中实现,按负担调整后的成功符合第2.4节。
就赢率而言,我们把每项主动政策重演一项任务与其所遵守的每项政策重演进行比较,将赢率计为1、平局计为0.5、亏损计为0,并将这四项比较与任务得分进行平均比较(Vargha和Delaney,2000年)。
胜率是这些分数相对于任务的平均值.
我们通过双面标志测试来检验主动政策是否赢得了比失败更多的任务,而测试中将完全分数为0.5的任务排除在外,并在五个用户模拟器中应用Holm校正(Holm,1979年)。

Following SimulatorArena ( Dou et al., 2025 ) , we used an LLM judge (GPT-6 Luna) to test whether each user simulator could be distinguished from the real user.
The judge was given two versions of the same interaction, one with the real user and one with the simulated user, and decided which one involved the real user.
We perform this test at the turn-level and the session-level.
For the turn-level, we use the simulated replies and corresponding recorded replies for the replication test.
For the session-level, we use the recorded sessions and the replays performed with the observed-policy for the adaptation evaluation.
Due to the positional bias of LLMs, we ran each comparison twice with the versions in each position, and used the judge’s confidence to break the tie when it chose the same position both times.
We report the Turing distance, | p − 50 | |p-50| , where p p is the percentage of comparisons in which the judge identified the real user.
As seen from the results Table 8 , both versions of SWE-WhatIf had a lower Turing distance than the other user simulators at both levels.

We recruited participants through Prolific who were 18 or older, had recorded Claude Code or Codex sessions on their own computer, had an approval rate of at least 95%, at least 100 previous submissions, English as their primary language, and residence in the United Kingdom or the United States.
We screened out participants whose recorded sessions had no user message from which a replay could start.
Participants were paid £11 for about 70 minutes, including a wait of 20 to 40 minutes while the replays ran, £0.50 if screened out, and £3 if they withdrew during the study or their replays could not be run.
Participants took 51 minutes on average, so the pay of £11 was above the £9 per hour recommended by Prolific.

blocks.en:
For the start of each replay, we first identified user messages in each recorded session that were followed by at least three more exchanges (i.e., a user message and the agent’s response).
Among these messages, we used GPT-5.6 Luna to judge whether the participant had pushed back on the agent at each of these messages (Fig. 31 ).
If a pushback was found, the replays started from the earliest of these messages with pushback, and, if none was found, simply from the earliest of these messages.
For 6 of the 16 analysed participants, the replays started from a user message where the participant had pushed back on the agent.
A recorded session does not include its repository, so we reconstructed the starting environment by extracting the content of all files that the recorded agent read or wrote from the recording itself.
The starting environment had no installed dependencies, no network access, and no running services, and we told every agent so.
blocks.zh:
对于每次重播的开始,我们首先在每次录制的会话中确定用户信息,然后至少再进行三次交换(即用户信息和代理商的反应).
在这些信息中,我们使用GPT-5.6 Luna来判断参与者是否在每条信息中向代理人推后(图31).
如果找到一个推回,则回放开始于这些消息中最早的带推回,如果没有找到,则仅仅从这些消息中最早的开始.
对于16名被分析的参与者中的6名来说,重播是从一个用户信息开始的,当时参与者向代理人推后.
一个录制的会话不包括它的寄存器,所以我们通过提取录制代理从录制本身读取或写出的所有文件的内容来重建开始的环境.
开始的环境没有安装的依赖,没有网络接入,也没有运行服务,我们告诉了每个代理商。

blocks.en:
We built each intent model from the participant’s recorded session and its reconstructed starting environment, with the same drafting, reviewing, and revising agents as in our experiments (Appendix A.1 ).
The simulated user was the SWE-WhatIf user simulator, with its style profile.
A replay stopped after three replies from the simulated user, or earlier once every intent was satisfied or dropped.
blocks.zh:
我们从参与者的录制会议及其重建的起始环境建立了每一种意图模型,其起草、审查和修订代理人与我们的实验相同(附录A.1)。
模拟用户是SWE-What If用户模拟器,带有其风格配置.
一次重播在模拟用户三次回复后停止,或者在每次意向得到满足或放弃后更早.

blocks.en:
Each participant saw three agents, chosen by the harness that was used for the recorded session.
If participants were Claude Code users, they saw replays with Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Haiku 4.5 in Claude Code and GPT-6 Sol in Codex.
If they were Codex users, they saw replays with GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna in Codex and Claude Sonnet 5.5 in Claude Code.
Of the 16 analysed participants, 7 provided a Claude Code session and 9 a Codex session.

如果参与者是Claude Code的用户,他们在Claude Code和GPT-6 Sol中看到了与Claude Opus 5.5和Claude Haiku 4.5的重播.
如果他们是Codex的用户,他们在Codex中看到了与GPT-6 Sol和GPT-6 Luna的重播,在Claude Code中看到了Claude Sonnet 5.5.

blocks.en:
Participants answered six background questions after providing their session.
Of the 16 analysed participants, 4 were software engineers, 2 researchers, 1 a data scientist or ML engineer, 1 a student, 2 in other technical roles and 6 in non-technical roles.

blocks.en:
Before the session was sent to us, we replaced sensitive details (e.g., API keys, user names in file paths, email addresses and names in git author lines) with placeholders on the participant’s computer, and showed the participant each replacement.
We repeated the replacement after their sessions were uploaded to our server and the interface only uploaded the part of each session up to three exchanges after the last message from which a replay could start.
Once the replays were ready, we deleted the participant’s session and the intent model, style profile, and starting environment built from it.

blocks.en: C.1 Participant Information and Consent
blocks.zh: C.1 与会者的信息和同意

blocks.en:
The following text reproduces the study overview, session-selection instructions, and consent agreement shown in the study interface.
Researcher names, institutional details, contact information, and the approval reference are replaced with bracketed descriptions for anonymous review.
The questionnaire and replay interface are given earlier in this appendix.
blocks.zh:
以下文本转载了研究概览,会话选择指示,以及研究界面显示的同意协议.
研究人员的姓名、机构细节、联系方式和批准参考资料改为括号内的说明,供匿名审查。
问卷和重播接口在本附录的前面给出。

blocks.en: C.1.1 Study Overview
blocks.zh: C.1.1 研究概览

blocks.en: Plan for about 70 minutes in all: about 30 minutes of your own time, and a 20 to 40 minute wait while the replays run. During the wait you can do something else: leave the study tab open in the background and it notifies you when the replays are ready, or close it and come back with your results link.
blocks.zh: 计划总共约70分钟:约30分钟的自有时间,20到40分钟的等待时间为重播运行时间. 在等待期间,你可以做一些别的事情:在背景中打开学习标签,并在重播准备完毕时通知你,或者关闭它并带回你的成果链接.

blocks.en: Consent (about 2 minutes). Read what we collect, who reads it and how long we keep it, and agree.
blocks.zh: 同意(约2分钟). 阅读我们收集的东西,谁读它,我们保存多久,并同意.

blocks.en: Choose chats (about 3 minutes). See exactly what would be uploaded from each usable chat, and choose which to upload to our server.
blocks.zh: 选择聊天(约3分钟). 查看每个可用聊天中要上传的内容, 然后选择上传到我们的服务器 。

blocks.en: Background questions, then a wait (about 2 minutes, then 20 to 40 minutes) while we create the simulated you and run the three replays.
blocks.zh: 背景问题,然后是等待(大约2分钟,然后20至40分钟),而我们则创建模拟你并运行三个重播.

blocks.en: Compare the replays (about 20 minutes). Predict which agent will do best, read the replays side by side and mark each message from the simulated you, then rank the agents and rate the simulated you.
blocks.zh: 比较回放(约20分钟). 预知哪个代理公司会做得最好, 并肩阅读重播, 并标记每个来自模拟你的信息, 然后排序代理公司 并评级模拟你。

blocks.en: See which agent was which (about 3 minutes), beside your prediction, and answer two short questions.
blocks.zh: 除了你的预测之外 看看哪个特工(大约3分钟) 回答两个简短的问题

blocks.en: We pay you £11 through Prolific when you finish. The consent page lists every payment.
blocks.zh: 完成后我们付你11英镑 同意页列出每笔付款。

blocks.en: Your chats are uploaded to our server only to create the simulated you and run the three replays. Once the replays are ready, we delete your chats and the simulated you.
blocks.zh: 您的聊天被上传到我们的服务器上,只是为了创建模拟的您并运行三个重播. 一旦重播准备好 我们删除你的聊天和模拟你

blocks.en: From the chat we use, we keep your first message, a short summary of what happened before the message where the agents start, that message, a short summary of what you wanted from the replayed part, and the three replays (what the agents and the simulated you wrote, and what the agents did in the copy of your project).
blocks.zh: 从我们使用的聊天中,我们保留了你的第一个消息,一个消息开始前所发生的事情的简短总结,那个消息,一个你从重播部分想要的东西的简短总结,以及三个重播(代理和模拟你写的东西,以及代理在你的项目副本中所做的).

blocks.en: Your prediction, your marks on the simulated you’s replies, your ratings, your ranking and your written responses.
blocks.zh: 您的预测、模拟答案上的标记、收视率、排名和书面答复。

blocks.en: Your answers to the background questions.
blocks.zh: 你对背景问题的回答。

blocks.en: Your Prolific ID.
blocks.zh: 你的身份证明很好

blocks.en: We use all of this only to analyse the study’s results. It is never released as a dataset or shared outside the research team, apart from the AI model providers that run the replays. We publish only the results, such as figures, and short excerpts with nothing that identifies you.
blocks.zh: 我们只用所有这些来分析研究的结果。 除了运行重播的AI模型提供者外,它从未作为数据集发布或共享在研究团队之外. 我们只公布结果,如数字, 和简短的节录,没有识别你。

blocks.en: The consent page says who reads this and how long we keep it.
blocks.zh: 同意书上写着谁读这个,我们保存多久。

blocks.en: C.1.2 Session Selection
blocks.zh: C.1.2 会话选择

blocks.en: Select each chat you’re comfortable uploading to our server. We replay one of them. After you upload, our server checks your chats once more. If it can’t use the first, it tries the next, so uploading more than one helps. Chats we don’t use are deleted once the replays are ready.

blocks.zh: 在上传任何信息之前,我们的网站会删除您聊天时的敏感细节,包括密钥,密码,您的用户名和电子邮件地址,并将一个占位符放在他们的位置上.

blocks.en: Our server sends the chats to OpenAI and to Amazon Web Services, which runs Anthropic’s Claude models. Both process them in the United States.
blocks.zh: 我们的服务器将聊天发送到OpenAI和运行Anthropic Claude模型的Amazon Web Services。 两者都在美国进行处理。

blocks.en: An OpenAI model reads whether you pushed back on or corrected the agent at each marked message. We prefer a message where you did, and otherwise use one of the marked messages. The models then create the simulated you from that chat.
blocks.zh: 一个 OpenAI 模型读取您是否在每条标记消息中 推回或更正代理 。 我们更喜欢用你写的地方的信息, 或者用一个标记的信息。 模型然后从聊天中创建模拟你。

blocks.en: Three coding agents then continue that chat from that message. Each works on a copy of the files the chat showed, in its own isolated container that can reach only its model provider.
blocks.zh: 然后三个编码代理 继续从消息的聊天。 每一个都工作在聊天所显示的文件的副本上,在自己的孤立容器中,只能接触到它的模型提供者.

blocks.en: OpenAI doesn’t use this data to train its models, and keeps it for up to 30 days to detect abuse. Amazon Web Services doesn’t store it and doesn’t share it with Anthropic.
blocks.zh: OpenAI不使用这些数据来训练模型, Amazon Web Services不存储,

blocks.en: The researchers running the study read what we keep (part 5) and your answers.
blocks.zh: 研究的研究人员读了我们保存的(第5部分)和你的答案.

blocks.en: Once the three replays are ready, we delete everything you uploaded and everything made from it, including the simulated you. We keep, for 2 years after the study ends, your first message, a short summary of what happened before the message where the agents start, that message, a short summary of what you wanted from the replayed part, and the three replays (what the agents and the simulated you wrote, and what the agents did in the copy of your project), and your answers. Then we delete them. If our server stops with an error, we keep what you sent until we have looked at the error, then delete it. We use them only for this research. Apart from the model providers in part 4, we don’t share them with anyone outside the research team, and we never publish or release them as a dataset. We publish only the study’s results: figures, and short excerpts with nothing that identifies you. Before publishing an excerpt, we remove names, user names, email addresses and file paths from it. We delete them sooner whenever you ask.
blocks.zh: 一旦三部重播准备好,我们删除你上传的所有内容和从中制作的所有内容,包括模拟的你. 在研究结束后的两年里, 我们保留了你的第一个信息, 简略地总结了在信息开始之前发生的事情, 简略地总结了您想要从重播的部分, 以及三个重播( 代理和模拟的你写了什么, 以及代理在项目副本中做了什么), 以及您的答案。 然后删除它们。 如果我们的服务器出现错误而停止, 我们保留您发送的, 直到我们查看错误, 然后删除它 。 我们只用它们来研究 除了第4部分的模型提供者之外, 我们不与研究团队以外的任何人分享, 我们只发表研究结果:数字, 和简短的节录, 没有识别你。 在发布节录之前,我们从中去除名字,用户名,电子邮件地址和文件路径. 每当你问起,我们就删除它们。

blocks.en: Taking part is voluntary. You can stop at any time without giving a reason and without any disadvantage. Until you finish the study, you can withdraw with the Withdraw and delete my data button at the top right of every page after you upload your chats. After you finish, contact the researchers ([researcher contact]) to have your data deleted.
blocks.zh: 参加是自愿的。 你可以随时停下来 不给任何理由 也没有任何缺点 在您完成研究之前, 您可以在您上传您的聊天内容后, 在每页右上方退出并删除我的数据按钮 。 完成后,请联系研究人员([研究者联系])删除您的数据.

blocks.en: If you withdraw before finishing, we pay you £3 as a bonus through Prolific. If you ask us to delete your data after finishing, you keep your £11.

blocks.en: Withdrawing deletes from our server everything you uploaded, the three replays and your answers. You can also contact the researchers to have them deleted.

blocks.en: Copies the model providers already received are kept as part 4 says.
